analysis.title: US equity size and style: CIO View
key_insights: UBS CIO stays Neutral across size segments (large, mid, small) and favors diversified exposure over a significant tilt toward any one segment.
UBS CIO stays Neutral on both growth and value. It cites the trade-offs between the styles and unusually broad dispersion across investment factors as the reason for balanced exposure.
After the latest bout of tech-related volatility, small and mid-caps are outperforming large-caps year to date. Large-caps have more exposure to the AI-related companies in recent headlines.

UBS says the fundamental outlook for AI remains intact, but investors are likely to question the returns on future spend commitments of US hyperscalers and frontier labs more closely. Risk-reward for large-caps is described as more balanced.
Higher interest rates are a headwind for smaller companies, which tend to carry more leverage, rely more on floating-rate or shorter-maturity debt, and face higher financing costs.
Offsets for smaller companies are a broadening earnings recovery, stronger manufacturing activity, AI infrastructure spending and improved sentiment toward health care and biotech.
Large-caps have been better insulated by stronger balance sheets, better cash generation and sustained AI-related investment.

Near term, additional Federal Reserve rate hikes may keep constraining small and mid-cap relative performance by raising financing costs and pressuring leveraged and cyclical businesses. A meaningful growth slowdown would add to that pressure.

Longer term, resilient economic growth, broadening profit momentum and relatively low valuations could support small and mid-caps (Fig. 2: S&P 600 forward P/E relative to S&P 500 near historically low levels).

Value is comfortably ahead of growth year to date, broad-based across sectors. The drivers are resilient economic activity, recovering manufacturing, strong energy performance and improving earnings across cyclical industries.
Value tech has substantially outperformed growth tech. Growth's valuation premium (Russell 1000 Growth vs Value relative forward P/E) has compressed to below historical averages (Fig. 3).
Value should keep benefiting if economic and earnings growth broadens. A sharper slowdown or sustained pressure from elevated oil prices would hurt cyclical companies.

Growth is supported by superior earnings momentum (Fig. 4), durable AI spending and monetization trends. The largest growth companies have strong balance sheets that limit direct sensitivity to higher rates.

sector_views.rationale: Greater exposure to AI-related names under scrutiny and a more balanced risk-reward, offset by strong balance sheets and durable AI trends.
Higher rates and possible further Fed hikes weigh on financing costs, offset by broadening earnings recovery and low relative valuations.
Superior earnings momentum and AI spending, but the valuation premium has compressed and growth tech has lagged value tech.
Benefits from broadening economic and earnings growth, but exposed to a sharper slowdown or sustained high oil prices.

earnings_insights: Earnings momentum is broadening across S&P size indexes (Fig. 1, NTM EPS indexed, FactSet data as of 17 November 2026).
Growth earnings are still outpacing value on annual EPS growth (Fig. 4).
Earnings are improving across cyclical industries, which supports value.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Further hikes may raise financing costs for leveraged small and mid-cap companies and constrain their relative performance.
Sustained pressure from elevated oil prices would pose risks to cyclical companies and value stocks.

risk_factors: Additional Federal Reserve rate hikes raising financing costs for leveraged and cyclical companies.
A meaningful slowdown in economic growth.
Sustained pressure from elevated oil prices, which would hurt cyclical companies.
Investor questioning of the returns on future AI spend commitments by US hyperscalers and frontier labs.
charts_described: Fig. 1 shows S&P size indexes' NTM EPS, indexed, with earnings momentum continuing to broaden (FactSet, UBS, as of 17 November 2026).
Fig. 2 shows forward P/E for the S&P 600 vs the S&P 500, with small-cap relative valuations near historically low levels.
Fig. 3 shows Russell 1000 Growth vs Russell 1000 Value relative forward P/E, with the growth valuation premium below historical averages.
Fig. 4 shows annual EPS growth, with growth earnings still outpacing value.
vol_and_positioning: The report cites tech-related volatility as the cause of the recent shift toward small and mid-caps. It gives no volatility levels.
UBS notes unusually broad dispersion across investment factors.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth, broadening profit momentum and relatively low valuations could support small and mid-caps over the longer term. Smaller companies also benefit from AI infrastructure spending and improved sentiment toward health care and biotech.
tension_points.bear_case: Additional Fed rate hikes would raise financing costs and pressure leveraged, cyclical businesses. A meaningful growth slowdown would add to the pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Additional Federal Reserve rate hikes or a meaningful economic growth slowdown would undermine the near-term case for small and mid-caps.

tension_points.bull_case: Value benefits if economic and earnings growth broadens. Growth has superior earnings momentum and durable AI spending, and its valuation premium has fallen below historical averages.
tension_points.bear_case: A sharper slowdown or sustained pressure from elevated oil prices would hurt cyclical companies and value. Growth tech has lagged value tech.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharper economic slowdown or sustained elevated oil prices would undermine the case for value.

theme_stances.key_argument: Balanced risk-reward across size segments favors diversified exposure over a significant tilt.
theme_stances.evidence: we favor diversified exposure rather than a significant tilt

theme_stances.key_argument: Trade-offs between the styles and broad factor dispersion make balanced exposure appropriate.
The AI fundamental outlook is intact, but investors will question returns on future hyperscaler and frontier lab spend.
